title: Kyverno controllers lose wildcard view permissions — generate / mutate / reports on custom resources need explicit RBAC

detection.reason: Kyverno's effective RBAC is not collected

quote: In 1.13 the wildcard view permission was removed and a role binding to the default `view` role was added.
remediation: If generate or mutate rules, or reports, cover custom resources, add get/list/watch for them under `admissionController.rbac.clusterRole.extraResources`, `backgroundController...` and `reportsController...` before upgrading. The upgrade guide shows the values that restore the old wildcard (not recommended).
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterpolicies.kyverno.io,policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.rules[]?.match | .. | .kinds? // empty | .[]] | any(test("\\."))) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row matches a kind with a group (Group/Version/Kind) — likely a custom resource
coversNotes: v1.13.0 Breaking Changes: This release contains the following breaking configuration changes
v1.13.0: Removal of wildcard permissions: prior versions contained wildcard
Breaking Changes: Removal of wildcard permissions

title: PolicyExceptions are no longer honoured in every namespace by default (CVE-2024-48921)

detection.reason: which namespace the admission controller accepts exceptions from (--exceptionNamespace) is a Helm value

quote: the Helm chart values of the prior versions enabled exceptions by default for all namespaces.
remediation: The 1.13 chart turns PolicyExceptions OFF (`features.policyExceptions.enabled: false`) and the binary honours none without an exception namespace (cmd/internal/engine.go@v1.13.0). Every exception stops exempting and the resources it covered start being blocked. Set `features.policyExceptions.enabled=true` AND `features.policyExceptions.namespace=<one namespace>` (move the exceptions there), or `namespace="*"` to keep the old, insecure behaviour.
verifyCommand: kubectl get policyexceptions.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"' ; kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.template.spec.containers[]; .image | test("(^|/)kyverno/(kyverno|background-controller|cleanup-controller|reports-controller)([:@]|$)"))) | select(any(.spec.template.spec.containers[].args[]?; test("^--?(enablePolicyException|exceptionNamespace)(=|$)"))) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # first block: every exception; second: the controllers passing --enablePolicyException / --exceptionNamespace
coversNotes: v1.13.0: Default exception settings: the Helm chart values of
Blog: Removal of insecure configuration for exceptions

title: 1.13 drops deprecated CRD versions — a version still in a CRD's storedVersions blocks the CRD update

detection.reason: read from each named CRD's status.storedVersions (version names only)

quote: Kyverno 1.13 drops deprecated API versions for its managed CustomResourceDefinitions.
remediation: If this fires, the 1.12 chart's migration hook did not collapse storedVersions (the 1.13 migrate hook runs post-upgrade, after the CRD update has already failed). Migrate manually before upgrading: rewrite the objects to the stored version (kube-storage-version-migrator, or `kubectl get … -o yaml | kubectl replace -f -`), then remove the dropped version from the CRD's status.storedVersions.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.group | test("^kyverno\\.io$")) | "\(.metadata.name) served=\([.spec.versions[] | select(.served) | .name] | join(",")) stored=\(.status.storedVersions | join(","))"'  # each row is a kyverno.io CRD with the versions it serves and still stores

title: The admissionreports / backgroundscanreports CRDs are removed

detection.reason: reads whether the old intermediate report CRDs are still installed

quote: Removed old intermediate reports types `admissionreports` and `backgroundscanreports` (#10083, #10500, #10504)
remediation: After the upgrade, delete the leftover (cluster)admissionreports / (cluster)backgroundscanreports CRDs; 1.13 uses ephemeralreports.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o name | grep -E 'admissionreports|backgroundscanreports'  # each row is a leftover CRD
coversNotes: v1.13.0 Changed: Removed old reports from Helm chart and disable

title: `--reportsChunkSize` is removed — a reports controller still passed it refuses to start

detection.reason: the 1.10-1.12 charts render --reportsChunkSize on every install and the 1.13 chart drops it itself, so the flag on today's Deployment says nothing about the upgraded one

remediation: Only a flag passed outside the chart's own rendering breaks: check `reportsController.extraArgs`, kustomize patches and hand-maintained manifests for `--reportsChunkSize` and remove it before upgrading. A plain Helm or release-manifest upgrade drops it (v1.12.7 `_helpers.tpl` renders it, v1.13.0 does not).
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.template.spec.containers[]; .image | test("(^|/)kyverno/(kyverno|background-controller|cleanup-controller|reports-controller)([:@]|$)"))) | select(any(.spec.template.spec.containers[].args[]?; test("^--?reportsChunkSize(=|$)"))) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row passes the flag today; it matters only if it does not come from the chart

title: The chart's `cleanupJobs` values are removed
quote: Removed cleanupJobs keys from Helm chart (#11242)
remediation: Drop `cleanupJobs.*` from your values; the report and UpdateRequest cleanup CronJobs are gone (circuit breakers replace them).
verifyCommand: helm list -A -o json | jq -r '.[] | select(.chart | test("^kyverno-[0-9]")) | "\(.namespace)/\(.name) \(.chart) app \(.app_version)"'  # each row is a Kyverno Helm release; read its values with: helm get values NAME -n NAMESPACE
coversNotes: v1.13.0 Changed: Removed cleanup cronjobs for updaterequests and ephemeralreports (#10249

title: Spec-level `validationFailureAction` (and its overrides, mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate, generateExisting) are deprecated — set them per rule

detection.reason: read from each policy's spec-level validationFailureAction; the CRD defaults it to Audit on every stored policy, so only an explicit Enforce is counted

remediation: Move `validationFailureAction` / `validationFailureActionOverrides` into each validate rule as `failureAction` / `failureActionOverrides`, and `mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate` / `generateExisting` into the rule's mutate / generate block.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterpolicies.kyverno.io,policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select((.spec.validationFailureAction // "") | test("(?i)enforce")) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row enforces through the spec-level action

title: Policy `.status.ready` is deprecated — read the Ready condition

detection.reason: tooling that reads policy status lives outside the cluster

remediation: Change scripts, dashboards and GitOps health checks that read `.status.ready` to read the `Ready` condition in `.status.conditions`.

title: Every rule must have a `match` block

detection.reason: rule match blocks are not collected as such

quote: Fixed an issue to make `match` field required in rule API (#11048)
remediation: Add a `match` block to any rule that has none; such a policy is refused on create/update.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterpolicies.kyverno.io,policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.rules[]?; .match == null)) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row has a rule without match
